title: Torre Centinela: Inauguration Marked by Absences and Criticism
author: José Shaddai Olvera Torres
content:
_This article by[José Shaddai Olvera
Torres](https://elchamuco.com.mx/author/shaddai/) originally appeared in the
[September 11, 2026 edition of El
Chamuco](https://elchamuco.com.mx/2026/09/11/torre-centinela-chihuahua-
inauguracion/), a Mexican leftist satirical political magazine._

![El Fisgón cartoon: Governor María Eugenia Campos beside the Chihuahua coat
of arms, asking whether the US agents in Chihuahua refer to
her](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/2026-09-12-torre-
centinela-inauguration-large.jpg)"When they ask what US agents are doing in
Chihuahua… do they mean me?" Cartoon: El Fisgón

The governor of Chihuahua, María Eugenia Campos Galván, inaugurated the Torre
Centinela, one of the emblematic projects of her security strategy, amid
questions over its cost, delay, and lack of coordination with federal and
municipal authorities.

**President Claudia Sheinbaum did not attend the event** , nor did members of
her security cabinet, despite the fact that officials from the Secretariat of
Defense, the Navy, Security and Citizen Protection, and the Attorney General's
Office had been invited.

In contrast, authorities from the United States embassy and consulate were
present, as well as representatives of the government of Las Cruces, New
Mexico.

## Ciudad Juárez Municipality Questions Lack of Coordination

The absence of the Ciudad Juárez municipal government also marked the
inauguration.

The acting mayor, Héctor Ortiz Orpinel, explained that he decided not to
attend due to the lack of coordination with the state government to access the
cameras of the video surveillance system.

Ortiz Orpinel noted that the municipality remains willing to collaborate, but
currently does not have access to that equipment.

![Screenshot from coverage of the Torre Centinela
inauguration](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/09/02-juarez-mayor.png)

The episode highlights one of the main questions surrounding the Torre
Centinela: coordination among the institutions that should be integrated into
the state security scheme.

## A 4.7-Billion-Peso Project

Construction of the Torre Centinela began in August 2022 and was completed
**two years behind schedule**.

The stated cost of the project amounts to **4.7 billion pesos**.

The former mayor of Ciudad Juárez, Cruz Pérez Cuéllar, described the project
as a "pharaonic work" and questioned the allocation of millions in resources
to infrastructure whose usefulness, he maintained, remains debatable against
other needs of the population.

## The Relationship with United States Security Agencies

The relationship with U.S. agencies has also been part of the project.

This past April, the state Secretary of Public Security, Gilberto Loya Chávez,
proposed using the 18th floor of the tower to house analysts and technical
personnel from the DEA, FBI, CBP, and HSI.

The invitation was later withdrawn, after news emerged of the deaths of two
CIA agents who were carrying out undercover work in the municipality of
Morelos, in the Sierra Tarahumara.

![Screenshot from coverage of the Torre Centinela
inauguration](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/09/03-consul-beamer.png)

Despite this, Katharine Beamer, the United States consul general in Ciudad
Juárez, was present at the inauguration, and she congratulated the Campos
government and considered that the tower will contribute to strengthening the
region's security capabilities.

During the ceremony, Campos defended the project as one of the legacies of her
administration and accused authorities and politicians, without directly
identifying whom she meant, of supposedly not being willing to defend "life
and peace."

## Rain, Wind, and Damage During the Inauguration

The event included a light and fireworks show under Campos's slogan:
"Sentinel, activate."

However, the display was affected by weather conditions.

Heavy rain and wind gusts of up to 75 kilometers per hour scattered the
attendees, knocked down screens installed for the show, and damaged sound and
lighting equipment.

In addition, one of the glass panels of the façade shattered.

## Thousands of Surveillance Devices

The Torre Centinela has 20 floors and three C7 command centers, connected to
thousands of surveillance devices.

The system includes:

  * 2,985 rotating and zoom cameras
  * 4,717 fixed cameras
  * 1,791 license plate readers
  * Highway arches
  * Drones
  * Video surveillance trailers

![Screenshot from coverage of the Torre Centinela
inauguration](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/09/04-tower-system.png)

The 18th floor will function as a fusion center to gather and process
information coming from municipal, state, and federal agencies and, through
the corresponding protocols, from international bodies.

Campos asserted that the inauguration does not simply represent the opening of
a building, but the consolidation of a project that will leave a legacy for
Chihuahua.

However, the project's delay, its cost, the questions over coordination with
municipal authorities, and the absence of the federal government place under
scrutiny an infrastructure that the state administration intends to turn into
a centerpiece of its security strategy.
